agree.reason: The open cost breakdown and the plain admission that the 23 ratings are a small sample will earn some trust, but this reader lost $85 on a funded project that never shipped, and nothing here addresses whether this one will ship.

honest.reason: It drops the 'proven hit' framing and states the small sample openly, though 'each of those 140 sessions changed something' and 'want to play it again' go a little past what the brief supports.

works_the_facts.reason: Cost per copy, about 572 backers needed, total shipping and the leftover margin are all correctly derived, but it never sets the 572 backers against the 1,240 sign-ups (about 46% conversion) or works out the roughly $28 left per copy.

right_comparison.reason: The only alternative it describes is the campaign failing to fund with no one charged, which costs this reader nothing; the outcome they actually fear, a funded project that doesn't deliver, is never described.

qualification.reason: The funding threshold names a number and a consequence, but the margin for 'things that always go wrong' is vague, there is no date for anything, and it never says what happens to the roughly 928 copies beyond the 572 backers.

objections.reason: It meets the first-time-creator objection with numbers, but it answers 'what if it doesn't fund?', which the all-or-nothing model already settles, instead of 'what if it funds and doesn't ship?'

fit.reason: It is a crowdfunding pitch of about 530 words, close to the 500 asked for, and it rightly declines the unsupported 'proven hit' claim while keeping the persuasive tone.
